name: Frontier Data Science and Machine Learning Papers
scope: Thirty peer-reviewed or explicitly flagged preprint records spanning statistical learning, causal inference, uncertainty, time series, tabular/data-centric AI, AutoML, recommender systems, graph ML, federated learning, privacy/fairness, MLOps/evaluation, and decision-making/RL.
methodology: Selected 2025-2026 frontier papers from official OpenReview, NeurIPS, ICML/PMLR, and ICLR records and paired them with influential foundations.

Cross-checked titles, author lists, venue/status, abstracts, and links against official proceedings pages, OpenReview, PMLR, ACM, AAAI, arXiv, Google Scholar/Semantic Scholar-indexed search results, and verified GitHub repositories.
A URL is listed only when its landing page or repository was directly checked; missing code/data is represented as an empty artifact list rather than inferred.
Preprints and vendor-authored or industrial benchmarks are explicitly flagged in provenance; acceptance status is taken from the venue/proceedings record, not from the arXiv version.

access_legend.null_meaning: No value was verified at the cutoff.

records.title: Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt
records.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)
records.contribution: Unified double-descent behavior across model size, sample size, and training time, challenging the classical U-shaped risk picture for modern overparameterized learners.
records.limitations: Primarily empirical; results depend on architecture, regularization, label noise, and training protocol and do not provide a complete finite-sample theory.
records.research_relevance: A foundational reference for scaling laws, benign overfitting, interpolation regimes, and the statistical theory of deep learning.

records.title: On the sample complexity of semi-supervised multi-objective learning
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
records.publication_status: peer-reviewed conference paper; NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight Poster
records.contribution: Separates when extra unlabeled data can reduce labeled-sample requirements in multi-objective learning from settings in which joint-model complexity creates an unavoidable statistical cost.
records.limitations: Results are loss- and assumption-specific; practical pseudo-labeling can degrade under distribution shift or poorly calibrated individual-task predictors.
records.research_relevance: Connects modern multi-task/foundation-model training with classical statistical efficiency and motivates principled use of unlabeled data.

records.title: Estimating individual treatment effect: generalization bounds and algorithms
records.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 70

access.paper_license: PMLR open access; copyright retained by authors

records.contribution: Formalized ITE estimation error through a bound involving factual loss and treatment-group representation discrepancy, leading to CFRNet/TARNet.
records.limitations: Assumes ignorability and overlap; unmeasured confounding, high-dimensional text/images, and policy deployment remain outside the core guarantee.
records.research_relevance: A standard baseline and theoretical bridge between representation learning and personalized causal effect estimation.

records.title: Conformal Prediction for Causal Effects of Continuous Treatments
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
records.contribution: Extends finite-sample, distribution-free prediction intervals to potential outcomes under continuous doses, making uncertainty explicit for dose-response decisions.
records.limitations: Coverage still relies on exchangeability/weighted-exchangeability and causal identification assumptions; intervals can become conservative when overlap is weak.
records.research_relevance: Directly supports safer personalized dosing and policy evaluation where point estimates of treatment response are insufficient.

records.title: Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)

access.paper_license: NeurIPS open access; license not stated on landing page

records.contribution: Established a practical, non-Bayesian baseline that improves predictive uncertainty and robustness by combining multiple independently optimized networks.
records.limitations: Training and inference cost scale with ensemble size; diversity is heuristic and does not guarantee calibrated or robust uncertainty under severe shift.
records.research_relevance: Remains the reference baseline for calibration, OOD detection, active learning, and uncertainty-aware decision systems.

records.title: Conformal Structured Prediction
records.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)
records.contribution: Addresses the combinatorial explosion of conformal prediction sets when outputs are structured objects, providing calibrated sets with practical optimization procedures.
records.limitations: Optimization complexity and set size remain task dependent; marginal coverage need not imply conditional coverage for every structured subgroup.
records.research_relevance: Important for reliable ML systems whose outputs are plans, sequences, graphs, rankings, or other structured decisions rather than scalar labels.

records.title: Informer: Beyond Efficient Transformer for Long Sequence Time-Series Forecasting
records.venue: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.publication_status: peer-reviewed conference paper; AAAI 2021 Outstanding Paper

access.paper_license: AAAI open access; license shown by venue page

records.contribution: Reduced the cost of applying transformers to very long forecasting horizons and became a widely reproduced long-sequence benchmark model.
records.limitations: Later work showed that simpler linear models can outperform it on some long-horizon benchmarks; architectural gains are sensitive to splits and evaluation protocols.
records.research_relevance: A seminal reference point for efficient temporal attention and for scrutinizing modern time-series foundation models.

records.title: Timer-XL: Long-Context Transformers for Unified Time Series Forecasting
records.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)

access.data_access: repository links to OpenLTM, checkpoints, and public datasets

records.contribution: Casts univariate, multivariate, and covariate-informed forecasting as a unified long-context next-token problem and reports strong task-specific and zero-shot results.
records.limitations: Long-context attention remains compute intensive; pretrained-data composition and leakage controls need careful auditing when comparing against benchmark-specific models.
records.research_relevance: A leading 2025 architecture for studying whether time-series foundation models generalize beyond narrow benchmark suites.

records.title: Why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on typical tabular data?
records.venue: NeurIPS 2022 Datasets and Benchmarks

access.data_access: public tabular datasets with repository loaders

records.contribution: Demonstrated that tuned tree ensembles remain strong on medium-sized heterogeneous tabular data and identified smoothness/rotation properties that disadvantage standard deep models.
records.limitations: Does not settle large-scale, multimodal, temporal, or text-heavy tabular settings; benchmark conclusions depend on tuning budget and dataset curation.
records.research_relevance: A data-centric baseline for evaluating tabular foundation models and AutoML claims.

records.title: ConTextTab: A Semantics-Aware Tabular In-Context Learner
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)

access.data_access: public benchmark datasets; model artifact in repository

records.contribution: Combines table-native in-context learning with semantic understanding and world knowledge through modality-aware embeddings and real-world tabular pretraining.
records.limitations: Performance depends on the availability and quality of meaningful column/table semantics; industrial deployment still requires privacy, leakage, and robustness audits.
records.research_relevance: Shows how data-centric metadata and semantic context can improve tabular foundation models beyond purely numeric encodings.

records.title: TabPFN: A Transformer That Solves Small Tabular Classification Problems in a Second
records.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)
methods: transformer pretraining on synthetic Bayesian priors
records.contribution: Reframed small-table classification as amortized Bayesian inference, obtaining fast predictions competitive with heavily tuned baselines.
records.limitations: Original version targets small classification tables and does not directly cover large datasets, regression, drift, or rich text/categorical semantics.
records.research_relevance: A foundational tabular foundation-model paper linking AutoML, Bayesian model averaging, and in-context learning.

records.title: Efficient Neural Architecture Search via Parameters Sharing
records.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 80
records.publication_status: peer-reviewed conference paper; official PMLR title uses 'Parameters Sharing'

access.paper_license: PMLR open access; copyright retained by authors

records.contribution: Reduced architecture-search cost by orders of magnitude through parameter sharing across candidate architectures.
records.limitations: Weight sharing introduces ranking bias and may not predict independently trained architecture performance; search remains task and controller dependent.
records.research_relevance: A key bridge from expensive NAS to one-shot and differentiable AutoML methods.

records.title: AutoML-Agent: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Full-Pipeline AutoML
records.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 267

access.paper_license: PMLR open access; copyright retained by authors

records.contribution: Automates data analysis, model selection, implementation, evaluation, and iteration through coordinated LLM agents rather than optimizing a single pipeline component.
records.limitations: Agent runs can be costly and nondeterministic; generated pipelines require security, leakage, and reproducibility checks before production use.
records.research_relevance: Defines a 2025 frontier for agentic, end-to-end AutoML and raises new evaluation questions beyond leaderboard accuracy.

records.title: Neural Collaborative Filtering
records.venue: International World Wide Web Conference (WWW)

access.paper_access: publisher landing page; access may vary
access.data_access: MovieLens public; Pinterest data described in repository

records.contribution: Replaced the fixed inner product of matrix factorization with learned neural interaction functions, establishing an influential deep recommender baseline.
records.limitations: Later studies showed results are sensitive to negative sampling, splits, and tuning; the model uses IDs and does not directly handle rich context or sequential behavior.
records.research_relevance: A foundational baseline for neural recommendation and for modern critiques of recommender evaluation protocols.

records.title: RecFlow: An Industrial Full Flow Recommendation Dataset
records.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)
records.publication_status: peer-reviewed conference paper; ICLR 2025 Poster; industrial benchmark
benchmarks: exposure, filter, recall, pre-ranking, ranking, and re-ranking stages

access.data_access: open via official repository under stated dataset terms

records.contribution: Releases a full-funnel, exposure-aware industrial recommendation trace rather than only the final clicked-feedback stage, enabling realistic multi-stage research.
records.limitations: The data reflect one Kuaishou application, period, and policy; privacy-preserving anonymization and policy confounding can limit generalization and causal interpretation.
records.research_relevance: A high-value 2025 benchmark for exposure bias, cascading selection, offline-to-online gaps, and full-funnel recommender evaluation.

records.title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
records.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)
records.contribution: Made localized spectral graph convolutions practical and popularized the modern GCN formulation.
records.limitations: Shallow neighborhood smoothing can over-smooth, struggle with heterophily, and scale poorly to dynamic or heterogeneous industrial graphs without extensions.
records.research_relevance: The canonical baseline from which message-passing, graph transformers, and graph foundation models descend.

records.title: AutoGFM: Automated Graph Foundation Model with Adaptive Architecture Customization
records.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 267

access.data_access: public graph benchmarks described in paper

records.contribution: Addresses the one-architecture-fits-all limitation of graph foundation models by disentangling invariant and variant graph patterns and customizing architectures across domains and tasks.
records.limitations: Customization introduces additional search/adaptation cost, and no official implementation was verified at the cutoff; broad-domain generality remains to be independently reproduced.
records.research_relevance: A leading 2025 signal that graph foundation models are moving from fixed pretrained encoders toward automated, data-aware adaptation.

records.title: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data
records.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS), PMLR 54

access.paper_license: PMLR open access; copyright retained by authors

records.contribution: Introduced FedAvg, showing that periodic averaging of locally trained models can reduce communication while tolerating non-IID client data.
records.limitations: Client drift under heterogeneity, partial participation, systems constraints, and privacy attacks require methods and safeguards beyond the basic algorithm.
records.research_relevance: The foundational algorithm and baseline for nearly all federated optimization, personalization, and privacy research.

records.title: Energy-based Backdoor Defense Against Federated Graph Learning
records.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)

access.data_access: public graph datasets described by repository/paper

records.contribution: Removes a clean/dirty validation-set requirement from prior federated graph backdoor defenses by using local trigger synthesis and energy-guided filtering.
records.limitations: Defense coverage is tied to evaluated trigger families and energy separability; adaptive attackers may learn energy-aligned or stealthier triggers.
records.research_relevance: Shows why federated learning, graph structure, and adversarial robustness must be evaluated jointly rather than as independent concerns.

records.title: Deep Learning with Differential Privacy
records.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

access.paper_access: publisher landing page; access may vary

records.contribution: Made rigorous per-user differential privacy practical for deep-network training through DP-SGD and tight privacy accounting.
records.limitations: Privacy amplification assumptions, group privacy, hyperparameter leakage, and severe utility loss at small epsilon require careful deployment analysis.
records.research_relevance: The standard algorithmic foundation for private deep learning and a prerequisite for modern private federated and foundation-model training.

records.title: Equality of Opportunity in Supervised Learning
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)

access.paper_license: NeurIPS open access; license not stated on landing page

records.contribution: Defined equalized odds and equality of opportunity and showed how optimal nondiscriminatory predictors can be derived from score functions.
records.limitations: Group parity definitions can conflict and do not resolve causal discrimination, measurement bias, intersectionality, or long-term feedback effects.
records.research_relevance: A canonical formalization that anchors fairness metrics, impossibility results, and responsible-ML evaluation.

records.title: Approximate Differential Privacy of the ℓ2 Mechanism
records.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 267
records.contribution: Provides tighter characterizations and computable bounds for the approximate-DP behavior of Gaussian/L2 mechanisms used throughout private ML.
records.limitations: Primarily a mechanism/accounting result; end-to-end privacy still depends on clipping, composition, implementation, and threat-model choices.
records.research_relevance: Improves the mathematical basis for calibrating noise and privacy budgets in DP training and analytics.

records.title: Fairness under Competition
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
methods: experiments with competitor strength and group size
benchmarks: ablations over applicant groups and competitor strength
records.contribution: Shows that independently fair algorithms can interact under competition to produce outcomes that differ from their isolated fairness properties.
records.limitations: Stylized utility and applicant models may not capture labor-market institutions, repeated feedback, or causal discrimination pathways.
records.research_relevance: Moves fairness analysis from a single deployed model to an ecosystem-level decision problem, an important frontier for policy and audits.

records.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)

access.paper_license: NeurIPS open access; license not stated

records.contribution: Named and taxonomized the maintenance, coupling, monitoring, and data-dependency risks that arise when ML models enter long-lived production systems.
records.limitations: Primarily experiential rather than a controlled study; modern LLM/agent operations require extensions to its original batch/supervised-system framing.
records.research_relevance: Still the conceptual foundation for MLOps, model monitoring, reproducibility, and lifecycle governance.

records.title: Datasheets for Datasets
records.venue: Communications of the ACM 64(12)
records.publication_status: peer-reviewed journal article; earlier versions circulated from 2018
methods: motivation, composition, collection, labeling, use, and maintenance sections

access.paper_access: publisher landing page; access may vary

records.contribution: Standardized dataset documentation as an engineering and governance artifact covering provenance, consent, labeling, intended use, and maintenance.
records.limitations: Self-reported datasheets can be incomplete or stale; the framework alone does not enforce correctness, privacy, or downstream compliance.
records.research_relevance: Foundational to data-centric AI, dataset audits, model evaluation, and regulatory documentation workflows.

records.title: Benchmark Health Index: A Systematic Framework for Benchmarking the Benchmarks of LLMs
records.venue: NeurIPS Evaluations and Datasets Track
benchmarks: 18 dimensions across design, implementation, execution, and transparency stages

access.paper_access: arXiv open manuscript; venue page indexed through OpenReview
access.data_access: framework and benchmark metadata in repository

records.contribution: Turns benchmark quality itself into a measurable object, revealing design, implementation, execution, and transparency gaps across widely used LLM benchmarks.
records.limitations: Index weights and domain coverage embed value judgments; scores can become stale as benchmarks are revised or contaminated.
records.research_relevance: A 2026 evaluation-governance framework for avoiding overclaiming from weak, contaminated, or poorly documented benchmarks.

records.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
records.venue: arXiv
records.publication_status: arXiv preprint; not peer-reviewed; vendor-authored OpenAI paper
records.contribution: Introduced a simple first-order policy-optimization objective that became a default RL and later RLHF algorithm.
records.limitations: Preprint status means there is no peer-reviewed venue record; benchmark tuning and implementation details substantially affect stability and reported gains.
records.research_relevance: Included deliberately as a clearly labeled vendor preprint because of its exceptional influence on deep RL and RLHF practice.

records.title: Soft Actor-Critic: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Stochastic Actor
records.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 80

access.paper_license: PMLR open access; copyright retained by authors

records.contribution: Combined off-policy sample efficiency with entropy-regularized stochastic policies, establishing SAC as a durable continuous-control baseline.
records.limitations: Simulation benchmarks do not capture all real-world safety and reset constraints; temperature tuning and reward scale strongly affect behavior.
records.research_relevance: A foundational bridge between probabilistic inference, exploration, and practical deep actor-critic control.

records.title: Adaptive Neighborhood-Constrained Q Learning for Offline Reinforcement Learning
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
records.contribution: Dynamically relaxes or tightens pessimism according to local data support, seeking better balance between in-distribution exploitation and out-of-distribution conservatism.
records.limitations: Neighborhood estimation adds hyperparameters and compute; performance remains benchmark- and dataset-quality dependent.
records.research_relevance: Represents the 2025 movement from uniformly pessimistic offline RL toward adaptive, state-dependent conservatism.

records.title: Causal Flow Q-Learning for Robust Offline Reinforcement Learning
records.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML)
records.publication_status: peer-reviewed conference paper; ICML 2026 regular paper

access.paper_access: arXiv open manuscript; ICML 2026 acceptance verified through ICML/OpenReview listing
access.data_access: public D4RL-derived benchmarks and generated confounded variants

records.contribution: Unifies causal hidden-confounder analysis with flow-based behavior modeling and robust offline value learning, extending DRO beyond observable uncertainty.
records.limitations: Guarantees depend on the assumed sensitivity parameter and causal structure; learned bounds can be loose or mis-specified in complex real systems.
records.research_relevance: A 2026 bridge among causal inference, uncertainty, and offline RL, directly relevant to high-stakes policies trained from observational logs.
